newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RED SOX BEAT YANKEES, ORIOLES LOSE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RED SOX BEAT YANKEES, ORIOLES LOSE.

text.p: Mo Vaughn's second clutch run-scoring single of the game scored Scott Hatteberg in the top of the 11th inning as the Boston Red Sox edged the New York Yankees 4-3 to keep their slim playoff hopes alive.
Heathcliff Slocumb (5-5), who allowed two runs to score in the eighth on a pair of wild pitches, worked 2-2/3 innings for the victory.
The Red Sox salvaged a split of the four-game series and moved within four games of Baltimore, which lost on Monday, for the wild card. Boston begins a two-game series with the Orioles on Tuesday.
Despite the loss, the Yankees reduced their magic number for clinching the American League East to three due to Baltimore's 8-7 loss to Milwaukee.
In Baltimore, Matt Mieske's two-out RBI single snapped a tie in the 10th inning and lifted the Milwaukee Brewers to an 8-7 victory over the Baltimore Orioles in a makeup game.
John Jaha had three hits, drove in four runs and scored three times as the Brewers won for the seventh time in 10 games.

"This is the way we are, the way we play," Mieske said. "This is our playoffs. We are playing to reach .500 ball and have to win the rest of our games to do it. We go to New York and plan on giving the Yankees all we can."
The Orioles remain four games behind the first-place New York Yankees in the American League East.
"Our bullpen has been used a lot lately and I guess it showed today," Baltimore manager Davey Johnson said.

In Cleveland, Manny Ramirez homered with two out in the eighth inning, and Jose Mesa tossed a scoreless ninth to lift the Cleveland Indians to a 7-6 victory over the Minnesota Twins for their 13th win in 15 games.

Cleveland, which already has clinched its second straight American League Central title, needs to win four of its last five games to become the first team since the 1980 Baltimore Orioles to have consecutive 100-win seasons.
At California, Chuck Finley scattered five hits over eight innings and Chili Davis belted a two-run homer as the California Angels got by the Seattle Mariners 4-3.
The loss keeps Seattle 1-1/2 games behind the Baltimore Orioles for the American League wild card berth and two games behind Texas for the lead in the AL West.
Finley (15-15) allowed a two-run homer to Jay Buhner and a solo blast to Ken Griffey Junior, walked three and fanned a season-high 11 to pick up his 14th win in 20 career decisions against Seattle.
In Oakland, John Wasdin won his first game in over a month and Ernie Young's RBI double snapped a tie in the second inning to lead the Oakland Athletics to a 5-3 victory over the Texas Rangers.
Wasdin (8-7) allowed two runs and eight hits through five-plus innings for his first win since August 8th. Bill Taylor struck out two in 1 2/3 perfect innings for his 16th save.

In Detroit, Robert Perez singled in the sixth inning to snap a tie and Erik Hanson allowed four runs over seven innings as the Toronto Blue Jays hung a 6-4 defeat on the Detroit Tigers, who matched the single-season club record for losses.
The Tigers (53-104) lost their 12th straight home game and equalled the dubious club record, set in 1952.

Hanson (13-17), who is tied with California's Jim Abbott for the most losses in the majors, allowed four hits, walked two and struck out seven. Mike Timlin struck out two in a perfect ninth inning for his 27th save.
At California, Chuck Finley scattered five hits over eight innings and Chili Davis belted a two-run homer as the California Angels got by the Seattle Mariners, 4-3.
The loss keeps Seattle 1 1/2 games behind the Baltimore Orioles for the American League wild card berth and two games behind Texas for the lead in the AL West.
